page: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel processor based on the Haswell architecture running at 2.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, meaning hyperthreading is disabled with a strict 1.0 thread per core allocation. It is equipped with 15.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core, and includes 100 GB of local SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate that the b2-15 sits on the lower end of the performance spectrum. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is in the bottom 10%, while multi-core CPU and Geekbench scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is also weak, though cached small-block reads and Passmark memory scores reach average levels. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and text processing perform at an average level, whereas static web serving and software compilation are weak.

Given the legacy Intel Haswell architecture and lower benchmark scores, this instance represents a budget-friendly option for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable resources, but do not demand high-performance compute. It is suitable for basic database operations, lightweight Redis caching, text processing, and general-purpose utility workloads. It is not recommended for intensive tasks like large-scale LLM inference, heavy compilation, or high-throughput web serving.
